author: Maya Lanzone
title: Walmart location admits it overcharged customers at checkout and says they're 'working to reimburse impacted shoppers' - NewsBreak
text:
By Maya Lanzone ,
14 hours ago
RETAIL behemoth Walmart has admitted to an overcharging error in the checkout section at one of its stores and is now working to fix the situation.
The sales tax errors forced customers to pay more than they had to , with one shopper calling attention to the overcharging on multiple of her receipts.
A Walmart shopper accused the retailer of overcharging on sales tax Credit: Hays Post Hays Post The Walmart store in question is located in Hays, Kansas, roughly 135 miles northwest of Wichita, which has been accused of charging consumers the incorrect sales tax .
Walmart corporate confirmed the error on Tuesday in an emailed statement to local news outlet Hays Post , although the company did not share a timeframe for the overcharging or note how shoppers could receive refunds .
“We deeply care about our customers, and we are working to reimburse impacted shoppers. We consistently seek to improve our processes to provide great customer service,” read the statement.
A Walmart shopper in Kansas , who asked to remain anonymous, reached out to Hays Post on Monday, accusing the Hays Walmart of making several sales tax errors on her receipts between August 13 and Saturday.
The shopper said she purchased $10 worth of merchandise via a self-checkout machine on Saturday and noticed it had overcharged her for sales tax.
In Hays, the sales tax is 9.25% on nonfood items and 2.75% on groceries. This excludes special sales tax zones, with the Walmart store not being in one of those zones.
The woman accused Walmart of charging her sales tax anywhere from 11% to 11.25%.
“This is just picking an arbitrary sales tax,” the shopper complained to Hays Post, adding that the food sales tax of 2.75% had not been applied to any of her receipts.
The woman visited the customer service desk after she first noticed the overcharging error, where a worker canceled the order and rang up the items again – and this time, the correct sales tax was charged.
“So then I got curious. I thought, man, if that’s happened to me, how many other people has that happened to?” the shopper told the Hays Post.
That’s when she checked previous receipts and noticed other instances when she had been charged the wrong sales tax.
In one $99 transaction, the woman said the sales tax was overcharged by $1.80.
The Walmart shopper returned to the Hays Walmart on Sunday afternoon to alert a manager of the issue.
She said that a customer service worker told her that the registers on the floor had recently been updated, but the customer service registers had not.
“I guess I thought people should know because that could have affected a lot of people. Yeah, and that could add up to a lot of money, even 1%,” the customer told Hays Post.
It’s not the first time that Walmart has charged shoppers the incorrect sales tax.
In January 2023, Kansas lowered the sales tax on food, and Walmart registers overcharged customers sales tax.
A similar incident took place in Alabama that same year.
In both cases, Walmart offered refunds to consumers.

Walmart corporate confirmed the error on Tuesday in an emailed statement to local news outlet Hays Post , although the company did not share a timeframe for the overcharging or note how shoppers could receive refunds .
